**Lebohang Morake** (born 11 July 1964),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-1) known as **Lebo M**, is a South African producer and composer, known for his songwriting and vocal work on the soundtracks to films such as _The Lion King, The Power of One_ and _Outbreak_ and numerous stage productions. He was recommended to Disney by Hans Zimmer, the composer of both adaptations of _The Lion King_, and formed and conducted the African choir that sang for the films.
Lebohang Morake was born on 11 July 1964 in Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa. With no formal training in music,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:2-2) he left school at the age of nine to perform music in night clubs.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3) Morake recorded his first single, "Celebration", when he was 13 years old, receiving only $20 for recording the record.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) When he was 13 years old, Morake became the youngest performer to sing at the nightclub Club Pelican, when he filled in for a backup singer who could not attend.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5)

In 1979, Morake sought to broaden his horizons, so he left by bus for Maseru, Lesotho, after hearing that a new club was going to be opening there.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) In Maseru, due to the apartheid system, he was under exile.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) At 15, he was working as a singer in the Victoria Hotel in Lesotho when Lesotho's Ambassador to the United States Tim Thahane noticed him and appreciated his musical abilities.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) Thahane helped Morake apply to the Duke Ellington School of the Arts, coordinating with the TransAfrica organization to send the singer to the United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-Billboard19980214-6) Morake lived at first in New York, again playing in restaurants and bars, and was supported by Black churches to attend music school.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) Morake moved to Los Angeles when he was 18 to pursue a music career.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-Billboard19980214-6)

In Los Angeles, he struggled to make ends meet, working odd jobs to survive while studying at Los Angeles City College.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:2-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) He performed sometimes at Memory Lane, a nightclub owned by Marla Gibbs.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) Morake was asked to help find a choir for the Oscars, so that they could perform music from 1987's _Cry Freedom_, a film about South Africa that was nominated for multiple Academy Awards, including one for Best Original Song.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3) He made further strides in his music career when by chance, he ran into childhood friend Solly Letwaba, who was the bassist for Johnny Clegg.

Letwaba introduced Morake to Clegg's producer, Hilton Rosenthal, who employed Morake as an intern and gofer for his production studio.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) Rosenthal was the music supervisor on the film _The Power of One_, and through him, Morake met the film's composer, Hans Zimmer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:2-2) After being asked about some ideas for the film's soundtrack, Morake ended up co-writing and co-producing the music for _The Power of One_ with Zimmer, helping to arrange the choruses.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) Morake used his knowledge of African rhythms to compose the soundtracks to other films, such as _Congo_ (1995), _Outbreak_ (1995), and _Born to be Wild_ (1995)_._[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) He decided to return to South Africa in the early 1990s, after the end of apartheid.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:2-2)
Morake wrote and sang the opening Zulu chant at the beginning of Disney's _The Lion King_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-7) for which he was sought by Zimmer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-Billboard19980214-6) He also contributed to the sequel to the film's soundtrack, _Rhythm of the Pride Lands_, and the film's direct-to-video sequel _[The Lion King II: Simba's Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King\_II:\_Simba's\_Pride "The Lion King II: Simba's Pride")_.

The duo composed so much music that Disney approved an additional soundtrack album, _Rhythm of the Pride Lands_, containing extra compositions.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3)_The Lion King's_original soundtrack, with the compositions that had made the cut for the theatrical release, earned the two composers a Grammy Award, and Zimmer won an Academy Award for Best Original Score.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3) Morake also helped score _The Lion King's_ stage musical, creating new music and adding pieces from _Rhythm of the Pride Lands_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) The musical was nominated for Best Original Score at the 52nd Tony Awards in 1998.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-8)
He founded the Lebo M Foundation and Till Dawn Entertainment._[citation needed_]
On 23 July 2019, Morake performed "Circle of Life" and "He Lives in You" at the opening ceremony of the 24th World Scout Jamboree._[citation needed_]
In April 2024, it was announced that Lebo M would join the music team for _Mufasa: The Lion King_, providing additional music alongside the film's songwriter, Lin-Manuel Miranda.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-10)

In 2026 Morake sued comedian Learnmore Jonasi for 27 million dollars, for making a joke about the lyrics of 'The circle of life'.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-12) After Morake dropped the suit, Jonasi’s legal team filed a motion under California’s anti-SLAPP statute. As a result, Morake was ordered to pay Jonasi's legal fees, totaling $40,000 as compensation for his legal expenses.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-thetab-13)

Morake was married to Viveca Gipson for 5 years. He divorced her and married Nandi Ndlovu and they were together for 11 years. He then divorced Ndlovu and married Angela Ngani-Casara for five years, from 2008 to 2013.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-15) Morake became engaged to Zoe Mthiyane but their relationship ended in 2016. He remarried his third wife, Angela, but they divorced again in 2017.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-dailysun.co.za-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-18) He lives with his family in Johannesburg and Los Angeles.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-dailysun.co.za-16) His daughter Refi is also a singer who often performs by his side.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-19) In April 2021,_[citation needed_] Morake got engaged to partner Pretty Samuels, in 2023 he had presumably filed for divorce.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-20)

Happy 62nd Birthday Lebo M!
Born on July 11, 1964, in Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa, Lebohang "Lebo M" Morake is the Grammy Award-winning producer, composer, arranger, and performer whose unforgettable voice helped define one of Disney's greatest musical masterpieces.
Recommended to Disney by legendary composer Hans Zimmer, Lebo M was brought on to help create the authentic African sound of The Lion King (1994). His powerful opening chant of "Nants ingonyama bagithi Baba!" at the start of Circle of Life has become one of the most iconic moments in Disney history, instantly transporting audiences to the Pride Lands.
Beyond lending his distinctive vocals, Lebo M assembled and conducted the African choir featured throughout The Lion King, helping create a soundtrack that won both the Academy Award and Golden Globe for Best Original Score. He also contributed to the companion album Rhythm of the Pride Lands, The Lion King II: Simba's Pride, the Broadway stage musical, and Disney's 2019 photorealistic remake of The Lion King.

More than three decades after The Lion King first roared into cinemas, Lebo M's unmistakable voice remains one of the most recognisable sounds in film history and continues to inspire audiences around the world.

texts.2: In Los Angeles, he struggled to make ends meet, working odd jobs to survive while studying at Los Angeles City College.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:2-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) He performed sometimes at Memory Lane, a nightclub owned by Marla Gibbs.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) Morake was asked to help find a choir for the Oscars, so that they could perform music from 1987's _Cry Freedom_, a film about South Africa that was nominated for multiple Academy Awards, including one for Best Original Song.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3) He made further strides in his music career when by chance, he ran into childhood friend Solly Letwaba, who was the bassist for Johnny Clegg.
texts.3:

The duo composed so much music that Disney approved an additional soundtrack album, _Rhythm of the Pride Lands_, containing extra compositions.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3)_The Lion King's_original soundtrack, with the compositions that had made the cut for the theatrical release, earned the two composers a Grammy Award, and Zimmer won an Academy Award for Best Original Score.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3) Morake also helped score _The Lion King's_ stage musical, creating new music and adding pieces from _Rhythm of the Pride Lands_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) The musical was nominated for Best Original Score at the 52nd Tony Awards in 1998.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-8)

Happy 62nd Birthday Lebo M!
Born on July 11, 1964, in Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa, Lebohang "Lebo M" Morake is the Grammy Award-winning producer, composer, arranger, and performer whose unforgettable voice helped define one of Disney's greatest musical masterpieces.
Recommended to Disney by legendary composer Hans Zimmer, Lebo M was brought on to help create the authentic African sound of The Lion King (1994). His powerful opening chant of "Nants ingonyama bagithi Baba!" at the start of Circle of Life has become one of the most iconic moments in Disney history, instantly transporting audiences to the Pride Lands.
Beyond lending his distinctive vocals, Lebo M assembled and conducted the African choir featured throughout The Lion King, helping create a soundtrack that won both the Academy Award and Golden Globe for Best Original Score. He also contributed to the companion album Rhythm of the Pride Lands, The Lion King II: Simba's Pride, the Broadway stage musical, and Disney's 2019 photorealistic remake of The Lion King.

Letwaba introduced Morake to Clegg's producer, Hilton Rosenthal, who employed Morake as an intern and gofer for his production studio.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) Rosenthal was the music supervisor on the film _The Power of One_, and through him, Morake met the film's composer, Hans Zimmer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:2-2) After being asked about some ideas for the film's soundtrack, Morake ended up co-writing and co-producing the music for _The Power of One_ with Zimmer, helping to arrange the choruses.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) Morake used his knowledge of African rhythms to compose the soundtracks to other films, such as _Congo_ (1995), _Outbreak_ (1995), and _Born to be Wild_ (1995)_._[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:1-5) He decided to return to South Africa in the early 1990s, after the end of apartheid.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:2-2)
Morake wrote and sang the opening Zulu chant at the beginning of Disney's _The Lion King_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-7) for which he was sought by Zimmer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-Billboard19980214-6) He also contributed to the sequel to the film's soundtrack, _Rhythm of the Pride Lands_, and the film's direct-to-video sequel _[The Lion King II: Simba's Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King\_II:\_Simba's\_Pride "The Lion King II: Simba's Pride")_.

The duo composed so much music that Disney approved an additional soundtrack album, _Rhythm of the Pride Lands_, containing extra compositions.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3)_The Lion King's_original soundtrack, with the compositions that had made the cut for the theatrical release, earned the two composers a Grammy Award, and Zimmer won an Academy Award for Best Original Score.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-:0-3) Morake also helped score _The Lion King's_ stage musical, creating new music and adding pieces from _Rhythm of the Pride Lands_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-SmithBillboard19980822-4) The musical was nominated for Best Original Score at the 52nd Tony Awards in 1998.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-8)
He founded the Lebo M Foundation and Till Dawn Entertainment._[citation needed_]
On 23 July 2019, Morake performed "Circle of Life" and "He Lives in You" at the opening ceremony of the 24th World Scout Jamboree._[citation needed_]
In April 2024, it was announced that Lebo M would join the music team for _Mufasa: The Lion King_, providing additional music alongside the film's songwriter, Lin-Manuel Miranda.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-10)

In 2026 Morake sued comedian Learnmore Jonasi for 27 million dollars, for making a joke about the lyrics of 'The circle of life'.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-12) After Morake dropped the suit, Jonasi’s legal team filed a motion under California’s anti-SLAPP statute. As a result, Morake was ordered to pay Jonasi's legal fees, totaling $40,000 as compensation for his legal expenses.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-thetab-13)

Morake was married to Viveca Gipson for 5 years. He divorced her and married Nandi Ndlovu and they were together for 11 years. He then divorced Ndlovu and married Angela Ngani-Casara for five years, from 2008 to 2013.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-15) Morake became engaged to Zoe Mthiyane but their relationship ended in 2016. He remarried his third wife, Angela, but they divorced again in 2017.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-dailysun.co.za-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-18) He lives with his family in Johannesburg and Los Angeles.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-dailysun.co.za-16) His daughter Refi is also a singer who often performs by his side.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-19) In April 2021,_[citation needed_] Morake got engaged to partner Pretty Samuels, in 2023 he had presumably filed for divorce.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebo_M#cite_note-20)

Happy 62nd Birthday Lebo M!
Born on July 11, 1964, in Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa, Lebohang "Lebo M" Morake is the Grammy Award-winning producer, composer, arranger, and performer whose unforgettable voice helped define one of Disney's greatest musical masterpieces.
Recommended to Disney by legendary composer Hans Zimmer, Lebo M was brought on to help create the authentic African sound of The Lion King (1994). His powerful opening chant of "Nants ingonyama bagithi Baba!" at the start of Circle of Life has become one of the most iconic moments in Disney history, instantly transporting audiences to the Pride Lands.
Beyond lending his distinctive vocals, Lebo M assembled and conducted the African choir featured throughout The Lion King, helping create a soundtrack that won both the Academy Award and Golden Globe for Best Original Score. He also contributed to the companion album Rhythm of the Pride Lands, The Lion King II: Simba's Pride, the Broadway stage musical, and Disney's 2019 photorealistic remake of The Lion King.

Lebohang Morake, aka Lebo M is a legend in South Africa’s entertainment scene. The 57-year-old musician, producer, composer, and arranger has been in the showbiz for over 25 years now and is one of the well-known names both in South Africa and Hollywood.
The award-winning star’s career and rise to stardom is quite intriguing, but so is his personal life. Lebo M has been in numerous interesting relationships throughout his life. He has been married four times-twice to the same woman, engaged once, and sired eight children, but unfortunately one of his children passed away.
Lebo M has a reality show called _Coming Home_that is aired on Show Max, which gives viewers a glimpse at his daily life as a musician as well as a family man. If you have been curious to know who Lebo M’s children are, then here they all are.
Read also: Musa Mseleku’s Fifth Wife.

## Zakiya
The first of Lebo M’s children is a daughter called Zakiya Naledi Morake who was born from his marriage with his first wife Viveca Gipson.
Zakiya celebrates her birthday every 11th of September but her age is currently unknown.
Zakiya lives in the United States but frequently visits her family in South Africa. Like the rest of her family, Zakiya also makes a few appearances on _Coming Home._

## Nthabiseng
The second of Lebo M’s children is also a daughter called Nthabiseng Morake who was also born during Lebo M’s first marriage to Viveca.
Nthabiseng lives with her older sister Zakiya in the US and she also makes a few appearances in _Coming Home._

## Refilwe
Refilwe Morake, also known as Refi, is Lebo M’s third daughter and first child with his second wife- Nandi.
Like her father, Refilwe is also a musician and has been singing since she was fourteen years old. Besides starring in her father’s reality show, Refi also dabbles as a vocalist, vocal producer and songwriter.
She recently toured and performed in Europe with her father in the Hans Zimmer Live concert.

## Tshepiso
The first born son and the fourth of Lebo M’s children is called Tshepiso Morake. Tshepiso is Refilwe’s full brother as they were both born to the same mother- Nandi.
Tshepiso is married to a woman called Ayanda and together they have a son called King. Since their relationship has never been approved by Lebo M, the two lovebirds decided to wed secretly at Home Affairs in 2021.
Lebo M considers Ayanda to be a gold digger and has refused to acknowledge her as his son’s wife, this has resulted in friction between Lebo and his oldest son.

## Thembalethu
Thembalethu Morake was Lebo M’s fifth child who was born during his marriage with Nandi and was full siblings with Refilwe and Thsepiso.
The late Thembalethu passed on when he was only 14 months old after drowning in their family swimming pool in their Dainfern home. The tragic incident occurred when the child was left under the care of a nanny while Nandi was attending a funeral and Lebo M was conducting auditions.
In 2021, Lebo M revealed that the autopsy results of his late son indicated that he had been molested first before being drowned. Thembalethu would have turned 20 years old in 2022.

## Letti
Nine-year-old Letti is the sixth of Lebo M’s children. She is Lebo M and his third wife’s daughter Angela.
Letti has half-siblings from both her mother and father’s side. From her mother’s side, she has a brother called Mthunzi and a sister called Ketso. Together with her mother and half-siblings, Letti appears on the family reality show- _Coming Home._

## Lulo
The youngest of Lebo M’s children is a five-year-old girl called Lulo who was born to Lebo M’s ex-fiance Zoey during their brief engagement which unfortunately did not end up at the altar.

## Lebo M’s stepchildren
In addition to Lebo M’s seven biological children, he also has two stepchildren through his third wife- Angela, from her past relationship.
He enjoys a very close relationship with his stepson– Mthunzi and stepdaughter Ketso. Ketso is a music prodigy and loves to play the piano with her step-dad.

Lebohang Morake, aka Lebo M is a legend in South Africa’s entertainment scene. The 57-year-old musician, producer, composer, and arranger has been in the showbiz for over 25 years now and is one of the well-known names both in South Africa and Hollywood.
The award-winning star’s career and rise to stardom is quite intriguing, but so is his personal life. Lebo M has been in numerous interesting relationships throughout his life. He has been married four times-twice to the same woman, engaged once, and sired eight children, but unfortunately one of his children passed away.
Lebo M has a reality show called _Coming Home_that is aired on Show Max, which gives viewers a glimpse at his daily life as a musician as well as a family man. If you have been curious to know who Lebo M’s children are, then here they all are.

## Zakiya
The first of Lebo M’s children is a daughter called Zakiya Naledi Morake who was born from his marriage with his first wife Viveca Gipson.
Zakiya celebrates her birthday every 11th of September but her age is currently unknown.
Zakiya lives in the United States but frequently visits her family in South Africa. Like the rest of her family, Zakiya also makes a few appearances on _Coming Home._

## Nthabiseng
The second of Lebo M’s children is also a daughter called Nthabiseng Morake who was also born during Lebo M’s first marriage to Viveca.
Nthabiseng lives with her older sister Zakiya in the US and she also makes a few appearances in _Coming Home._

## Refilwe
Refilwe Morake, also known as Refi, is Lebo M’s third daughter and first child with his second wife- Nandi.
Like her father, Refilwe is also a musician and has been singing since she was fourteen years old. Besides starring in her father’s reality show, Refi also dabbles as a vocalist, vocal producer and songwriter.
She recently toured and performed in Europe with her father in the Hans Zimmer Live concert.

The first born son and the fourth of Lebo M’s children is called Tshepiso Morake. Tshepiso is Refilwe’s full brother as they were both born to the same mother- Nandi.
Tshepiso is married to a woman called Ayanda and together they have a son called King. Since their relationship has never been approved by Lebo M, the two lovebirds decided to wed secretly at Home Affairs in 2021.
Lebo M considers Ayanda to be a gold digger and has refused to acknowledge her as his son’s wife, this has resulted in friction between Lebo and his oldest son.

## Thembalethu
Thembalethu Morake was Lebo M’s fifth child who was born during his marriage with Nandi and was full siblings with Refilwe and Thsepiso.
The late Thembalethu passed on when he was only 14 months old after drowning in their family swimming pool in their Dainfern home. The tragic incident occurred when the child was left under the care of a nanny while Nandi was attending a funeral and Lebo M was conducting auditions.
In 2021, Lebo M revealed that the autopsy results of his late son indicated that he had been molested first before being drowned. Thembalethu would have turned 20 years old in 2022.

Nine-year-old Letti is the sixth of Lebo M’s children. She is Lebo M and his third wife’s daughter Angela.
Letti has half-siblings from both her mother and father’s side. From her mother’s side, she has a brother called Mthunzi and a sister called Ketso. Together with her mother and half-siblings, Letti appears on the family reality show- _Coming Home._

The youngest of Lebo M’s children is a five-year-old girl called Lulo who was born to Lebo M’s ex-fiance Zoey during their brief engagement which unfortunately did not end up at the altar.

In addition to Lebo M’s seven biological children, he also has two stepchildren through his third wife- Angela, from her past relationship.
He enjoys a very close relationship with his stepson– Mthunzi and stepdaughter Ketso. Ketso is a music prodigy and loves to play the piano with her step-dad.

# Lebohang 'Lebo M' Morake, The Alchemy of Collaboration
## Lebohang 'Lebo M' Morake, The Alchemy of Collaboration
In this gripping episode of Listen To Your Footsteps, host Kojo Baffoe sits down with Grammy-winning composer Lebohang Morake, known the world over simply as Lebo M, the voice and vision behind some of the most celebrated music in cinematic and stage history. From his early days in Johannesburg to his groundbreaking work on The Lion King, Lebo M discusses the deep cultural roots of his music, his inspirations, and the personal and professional journeys that have shaped his illustrious career.He shares stories of the challenges he faced, the triumphs he celebrated, and the wisdom he’s gathered along the way. This episode is not just about music; it's about making a global impact while staying connected to one’s heritage. From his beginnings in Soweto’s Pelican Club to exile in Lesotho and global acclaim, Lebo’s journey is a testament to the power of intuition, passion, and unshakable authenticity. Key Moments: The Hustle Begins:At 14, Lebo became the youngest background singer in South Africa, thanks to a mother who “threw [him] at anything arts-related”—even when school wasn’t a priority. Exile & Survival:A gig in Lesotho turned into a political escape. “I collapsed at the Caledon River. They carried me across,” he recalls. His refugee hustle? Playing piano for ambassadors to fund his passage to America. The Power of Naivety:How a coffee-run kid co-composed The Power of One soundtrack without formal training. “Hans Zimmer’s orchestrators said, ‘Call a lawyer—that’s YOUR work.’” Lion King’s Magic:Lebo reveals the serendipity behind Circle of Life: “I was bored, humming over Hans’ chords. That ‘ahhh’? One take.” Broadway Revolution:Why The Lion King’s stage adaptation redefined African storytelling: “It was tech meets tradition—and it worked.” Parenting & Sacrifice:“My older kids grew up in hotels. I’m still making up lost time.” Lin-Manuel & Mufasa:Why he embraced the prequel: “If it’s Lin, I’m in.” Why Listen? Lebo’s story isn’t just about music—it’s about trusting your voice when no one else does.

# Lebohang 'Lebo M' Morake, The Alchemy of Collaboration
## Lebohang 'Lebo M' Morake, The Alchemy of Collaboration
In this gripping episode of Listen To Your Footsteps, host Kojo Baffoe sits down with Grammy-winning composer Lebohang Morake, known the world over simply as Lebo M, the voice and vision behind some of the most celebrated music in cinematic and stage history. From his early days in Johannesburg to his groundbreaking work on The Lion King, Lebo M discusses the deep cultural roots of his music, his inspirations, and the personal and professional journeys that have shaped his illustrious career.He shares stories of the challenges he faced, the triumphs he celebrated, and the wisdom he’s gathered along the way. This episode is not just about music; it's about making a global impact while staying connected to one’s heritage. From his beginnings in Soweto’s Pelican Club to exile in Lesotho and global acclaim, Lebo’s journey is a testament to the power of intuition, passion, and unshakable authenticity. Key Moments: The Hustle Begins:At 14, Lebo became the youngest background singer in South Africa, thanks to a mother who “threw [him] at anything arts-related”—even when school wasn’t a priority. Exile & Survival:A gig in Lesotho turned into a political escape. “I collapsed at the Caledon River. They carried me across,” he recalls. His refugee hustle? Playing piano for ambassadors to fund his passage to America. The Power of Naivety:How a coffee-run kid co-composed The Power of One soundtrack without formal training. “Hans Zimmer’s orchestrators said, ‘Call a lawyer—that’s YOUR work.’” Lion King’s Magic:Lebo reveals the serendipity behind Circle of Life: “I was bored, humming over Hans’ chords. That ‘ahhh’? One take.” Broadway Revolution:Why The Lion King’s stage adaptation redefined African storytelling: “It was tech meets tradition—and it worked.” Parenting & Sacrifice:“My older kids grew up in hotels. I’m still making up lost time.” Lin-Manuel & Mufasa:Why he embraced the prequel: “If it’s Lin, I’m in.” Why Listen? Lebo’s story isn’t just about music—it’s about trusting your voice when no one else does.

# Lebohang 'Lebo M' Morake, The Alchemy of Collaboration
## Lebohang 'Lebo M' Morake, The Alchemy of Collaboration
In this gripping episode of Listen To Your Footsteps, host Kojo Baffoe sits down with Grammy-winning composer Lebohang Morake, known the world over simply as Lebo M, the voice and vision behind some of the most celebrated music in cinematic and stage history. From his early days in Johannesburg to his groundbreaking work on The Lion King, Lebo M discusses the deep cultural roots of his music, his inspirations, and the personal and professional journeys that have shaped his illustrious career.He shares stories of the challenges he faced, the triumphs he celebrated, and the wisdom he’s gathered along the way. This episode is not just about music; it's about making a global impact while staying connected to one’s heritage. From his beginnings in Soweto’s Pelican Club to exile in Lesotho and global acclaim, Lebo’s journey is a testament to the power of intuition, passion, and unshakable authenticity. Key Moments: The Hustle Begins:At 14, Lebo became the youngest background singer in South Africa, thanks to a mother who “threw [him] at anything arts-related”—even when school wasn’t a priority. Exile & Survival:A gig in Lesotho turned into a political escape. “I collapsed at the Caledon River. They carried me across,” he recalls. His refugee hustle? Playing piano for ambassadors to fund his passage to America.
